bull.b: Strong sales growth combined with gross margins in the low-70% range indicates attractive product economics and effective demand conversion. If maintained, this combination can fund commercial investment, improve operating leverage, and support stronger earnings power over the next several quarters.

Momentum across several ophthalmic franchises reduces reliance on a single product and supports a broader commercial platform. Rising prescriptions, ordering accounts, surgical adoption and expanded PBM access can enlarge the addressable market and sustain revenue growth.

The shift to positive operating and free cash flow improves near-term liquidity and shows that cash conversion is strengthening alongside revenue. Sustained generation would give Harrow more capacity to fund operations, support launches, and gradually address its debt burden.

bear.b: Higher leverage and a thin equity cushion reduce financial flexibility if operating performance weakens. Debt-funded asset growth increases refinancing and potential dilution risk, while available cash generation must remain durable enough to support obligations and future investment.

Widening net losses indicate that strong revenue and gross margins have not yet translated into consistent bottom-line profitability. Operating costs or other headwinds remain substantial, limiting internal capital formation and making execution on the growth strategy more important.

The reimbursement change removes an important channel for IHEEZO and constrains adoption in ambulatory surgical centers. Although Harrow is pivoting toward in-office markets, the access loss can limit product penetration and create a lasting drag on demand in that setting.
